answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using time-locked staking bonds recorded in an identity atlas. Agents must deposit collateral that contracts slash if duplicate or collusive behaviors are proven. An attacker incurs an inescapable capital liquidity cost per identity, replacing the velvet ease of zero-cost cloning with financial risk. However, this mechanism favors wealthy operators, excluding underfunded agents from ecosystems that harbor high deposit thresholds.
